design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST
An asset manager rings to renew an agreement and asks for exactly two things: the price for the coming year and the further term actually recorded. She does not know, and the call gives her no reason to know, that coverage at her building was withdrawn six weeks ago for arrears her payables team never cleared. The whole of the work sits between her request and the policy: the renewal rule says outright that a further term is recorded only once the agreement stands back in force after a withdrawal of coverage, and the reinstatement rule says outright that the charge for restoring coverage is worked out only after the arrears standing on the agreement are answered by a payment recorded against the agreement as a whole rather than against any named invoice. Read hop by hop, that is a chain of three problems and three computations of four, five and six factors, with the arrears clearance reserved to the owner herself. The prize for missing it is a confident wrong number: an agent that prices the renewal straight off the computation document writes 12854, and one that reads the agreement's annual price and escalates it at the published rate writes something near 12854 too; gold is 10948, and the agreement is left standing in the renewal window on a further term rather than standing withdrawn.

SCOPE: OCCUPIED, CLAIMED, RESERVED
Task 0 occupied maintenance_ext_overdue_instalment_charge / charge_late_fee_06bbd225, maintenance_ext_unperformed_visit_credit / issue_visit_credit_1d93f422, maintenance_ext_additional_visit_charge / charge_extra_visit_764307e1 and maintenance_ext_account_settlement / record_agreement_settlement_0349d2fc — the ancillary-charge, missed-visit-credit, additional-visit and account-settlement space of a live, active agreement. This task claims the entirely separate lifecycle space that task 0 left alone: maintenance_ext_renewal_arrears_clearance / clear_agreement_arrears_489edb92, maintenance_ext_coverage_reinstatement / reinstate_agreement_coverage_5877576a and maintenance_ext_renewal_term_pricing / renew_agreement_term_748887d3, refining maintenance_billing_and_late_fee's payment-application clause, maintenance_suspension_and_reinstatement's reinstatement clause and maintenance_renewal's escalation clause. The two scopes share no policy and no tool. With both tasks closed the difficulty's seven extended policies are covered exactly once each.

THE STEP 0 DRAW, AS PRINTED
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/maintenance_agreement_desk --tasks 2
  {"task": 0, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/maintenance_agreement_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 5, 5]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "commercial_hvac_service_contractor/maintenance_agreement_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 4]}
The tree was designed to that draw: 2 prerequisite problems, 3 problems in all. Factor counts taken: the renewal price 6, the charge for restoring coverage 5, the arrears clearance 4 — the multiset {4,5,6} of the draw.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD
Root (what the caller's request points at): maintenance_ext_renewal_term_pricing, computing renewed_annual_price_usd, written by the desk through renew_agreement_term_748887d3.
The tree is a chain of three: the arrears clearance, then the reinstatement, then the renewal. Acyclic, every node reachable from the root, one topological order only.

Edge 1  renewal <- reinstatement
  kind state_gate; gate maintenance_agreements.status; form state.
  Prerequisite sentence (verbatim from the renewal policy's own rule): "A further term is recorded only once the agreement stands back in force after a withdrawal of coverage."
  Four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only once"; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — the agreement standing back in force after a withdrawal — named in the words the agreement record uses, with no action, performer or tool named; (3) no tool name, policy id, snake_case token or row id; (4) the strength is hard ("only once") and the scope is exactly a withdrawal of coverage, no wider and no narrower than the edge's condition.
  Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: only maintenance_ext_coverage_reinstatement moves an agreement out of a withdrawal, through reinstate_agreement_coverage_5877576a; no other policy of the charter restores withdrawn coverage.
  Derivation the reader performs: sentence -> "does the agreement stand back in force?" -> the agreement record shows status suspended, suspension_date 2026-10-08 and no reinstatement_date -> it does not -> the reinstatement policy's own rule says what the charge for putting coverage back in force is and that it is what restores it -> that is the write to make first.
  Condition: the agreement no longer stands in suspended status, having been put back in force after the withdrawal of coverage.
  Resolving action and owner: reinstate_agreement_coverage_5877576a, owner=agent.
  Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: initial_state.maintenance_agreements.<agreement>.status = suspended; .suspension_date = 2026-10-08; .reinstatement_date is empty.
  Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the reinstatement leaves the agreement standing suspended with no restoration day and no charge for restoring coverage; the terminal record differs in status, in reinstatement_date, in balance_due by 230.00 and by one missing charge row.

Edge 2  reinstatement <- arrears clearance
  kind value_input; gate: the reinstatement policy's compute binding settled_shortfall; form state.
  Prerequisite sentence (verbatim from the reinstatement policy's own rule): "The charge for putting coverage back in force is worked out only after the arrears standing on the agreement are answered by a payment recorded against the agreement as a whole rather than against any named invoice."
  Four-point test: (1) "only after"; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state — a payment entry standing on the agreement that names no invoice, set against the arrears — named in the words the payment ledger uses, with no action, performer or tool; (3) no tool name, policy id or code token; (4) hard ("only after"), scoped exactly to the arrears standing on the agreement and to a payment against the agreement as a whole.
  Exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: the account-settlement policy's tool always applies a payment to a named invoice, and only maintenance_ext_renewal_arrears_clearance books a payment against the agreement as a whole with no invoice named (its own rule opens on exactly that: taken as one figure against the agreement rather than invoice by invoice), through clear_agreement_arrears_489edb92. The state form was therefore available and is used (auditor's O-5).
  Derivation: sentence -> "does a payment against the agreement as a whole answer the arrears?" -> the ledger shows 10400.00 invoiced against 7020.00 received in seven payments, every one of them applied to a named invoice, the April one 260.00 short, a shortfall of 3380.00 -> no such payment stands -> the clearance policy's own rule computes the figure the owner clears the arrears at as one figure against the agreement and is the owner's own act -> that is the write, and the desk hands it over.
  Condition: the payments received on the agreement stand against the instalments invoiced on it at the shortfall the reinstatement fee is to be taken on.
  Resolving action and owner: clear_agreement_arrears_489edb92, owner=user.
  Seed evidence: initial_state.maintenance_events.<2026-10 instalment>.amount_usd = 1040.0 with no payment naming it; initial_state.maintenance_events.<April payment>.amount_usd = 780.0 against a 1040.00 instalment; initial_state.maintenance_agreements.<agreement>.balance_due = 3411.2.
  Deletion sensitivity: skipping the clearance leaves the charge for restoring coverage at 290.00 instead of 230.00 — the shortfall stays at 3380.00, more than one instalment, so the fee is taken in full rather than at the part cleared share.

Topological order: clearance, reinstatement, renewal. Being a chain there is nothing to reorder and prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness records that the order is entailed by the two prerequisite sentences themselves.
user_scenario mentions no prerequisite: see prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint. The tool layer validates none: see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block.
At least one problem is the customer's own write: the arrears clearance, clear_agreement_arrears_489edb92, is owner=user. The in-person semantics are genuine — it is Cedarloft's own money leaving Cedarloft's own bank, and the caller says outright she will move it herself rather than hand anyone the details. It completes on the spot: the tool books the payment and moves the balance synchronously under the one frozen clock.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD
Subject maintenance_payment_received (the clearance, step 7). Governing base policy: maintenance_billing_and_late_fee alone, which carries no eligibility gate on that subject, so it enters as policy_scope. What is still inherited and true here: payments are applied to what the agreement owes and the balance moves by the amount paid.
Subject maintenance_agreement_reinstated (step 9). Governing base policy: maintenance_suspension_and_reinstatement, whose gate reinstatement_inside_window (kind time) applies to that subject and is inherited verbatim; its other gate, arrears_beyond_suspension_period, applies to maintenance_agreement_suspended and does not bind here. Time gate detail, copied verbatim from base: anchor event "the term end date"; anchor source maintenance_agreements.term_end_date; relation not_after; duration from variants.expired_reinstatement_window_days, which is 60 for the Full Coverage Agreement; unit calendar_days; counting rule with the end day excluded and the final day included; boundary inclusive. Positive case: the term ends 2026-12-31, still ahead of the handling day of 2026-11-19, so the window counted forward from that end day has not begun to run and coverage may be restored. Negative case: had the term ended 2026-09-19, the 60 days counted forward with the end day excluded would have run out on 2026-11-18, one day before the handling day, and the correct answer would be to refuse and require a fresh proposal.
Subject maintenance_agreement_renewed (step 11). Governing base policies: maintenance_activation_and_entitlement (its two gates apply to maintenance_agreement_activated, so policy_scope here), maintenance_agg_multi_site_discount (no eligibility at all, policy_scope) and maintenance_renewal, whose two authorization gates apply to this subject and are inherited item by item. renewal_acceptance_on_file is satisfied by the intake record lodged 2026-11-04 with outcome confirmed against this agreement, correlated by maintenance_requests.agreement_id to the action's agreement_id. no_timely_non_renewal_notice is satisfied because the only intake record on the agreement is that renewal acceptance: no non-renewal notice exists, so none was received on or before the deadline, which for this tier would have been 60 calendar days back from 2026-12-31, that is 2026-11-01.
No time gate has been re-anchored: the only one in this task is the reinstatement window, deep-copied field for field.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
step 7 — the agreement account as a whole. The clearance policy's own rule states outright that a payment clearing the arrears on a suspended agreement is taken as one figure against the agreement rather than invoice by invoice, which is why the tool carries no invoice reference; the aggregation scope is the agreement and every row summed carries its id. Rows included in the arrears: the three instalments whose due days fall in the last three months (2026-08-31, 2026-10-01, 2026-10-31). Rows excluded: the seven earlier instalments and all seven payments, whose due and received days fall outside that window — the April shortfall of 260.00 is what makes that window differ from the whole-ledger reading.
step 9 — the agreement itself, correlated by maintenance_agreements.agreement_id. The visits counted as lost are narrowed to those booked for a day in the last three months with no completion in that window: WO-4250977 (booked and completed 2026-09-22) and WO-4251083 (booked 2026-10-20, nothing performed) are in the window, WO-4250894 (booked 2026-08-18, nothing performed) is outside it and is excluded by the window the rule sets.
step 11 — the agreement itself again, correlated by maintenance_agreements.agreement_id, with the renewal acceptance tied to it by maintenance_requests.agreement_id. The visits counted are the term's completions against the term's entitlement credit; the automation figures are read from the plan at the same building and from no other plan.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW EXISTS
customers / sites: the owner and the building. Remove either and the agreement has no object and no lookup can reach it.
maintenance_agreements: the agreement in play. status suspended and suspension_date 2026-10-08 are what falsify the renewal's gate and set the 42-day withdrawal that two ladders read; term_end_date fixes both the reinstatement window and the whole month of term left; annual_price_usd drives the escalation base, the instalment value and the renewal price; renewal_notice_date records that the withdrawal was made from inside the renewal window, which is what the reinstatement returns it to.
maintenance_events, 41 rows: the entitlement credit (10 visits — remove it and the renewal's base rule has nothing to compare the completions against); the repair allowance credit (keeps the agreement record self-consistent); ten monthly instalments whose due days fix the three-month arrears window; seven payments, the April one 260.00 short, which is exactly what makes the windowed arrears differ from the whole-ledger arrears and so what makes that factor bite; two charges for instalments left unpaid, which put the clearance share and the renewal escalation off their fall-through tiers; ten bookings and eight completions arranged so that one unperformed booking falls inside the three-month window and one outside it, which is what makes the lost-visit window factor bite and what leaves the term two visits short for the renewal base; two written condition reports against three preventive completions, which puts the report adjustment on its middle tier.
maintenance_requests: the renewal acceptance received 2026-11-04 with outcome confirmed. It is what satisfies both of maintenance_renewal's authorization gates before the write, and it is also the fact the caller states in her own words at the opening.
controls_plans: the owner's Remote Optimization Plan at the same building, active, 240 monitored points, 6.5 support hours, 3 alarm responses, nothing owing. Four cross-difficulty tiers rest on it: the standing allowance in the clearance (its balance), the plan discount in the reinstatement (its support pool), the portfolio discount in the renewal (its monitored points) and the bundle credit in the renewal (its alarm allowance). Change any one of those fields and the corresponding figure moves.
Automatic clauses checked before seeding: the suspension clause is already spent (coverage was withdrawn 2026-10-08, beyond the tier's 30 days from the 2026-08-31 due day) and this task discharges it rather than leaving it hanging; the for-cause cancellation clause bites only once the agreement has been left suspended beyond the tier's 42 days, that is from 2026-11-23, three days after the handling day, so the agreement stands reinstatable with a margin rather than on the boundary (the auditor's boundary observation); the renewal window opened 2026-10-02 and is carried by this task's root; no covered repair has been applied, so the allowance clause is quiet. No cache trap is used: visits_remaining (2), repair_allowance_remaining (12500.00) and balance_due (3411.20) all agree with their ledgers at the opening.

PERSONA DESIGN
Priya Raghunathan is written as the asset manager rather than the payer: warm, quick, reading from a renewal tracker she keeps herself, and openly without sight of what payables does with the invoices. Volunteered at the opening: the company, the building, the surface goal (carry the agreement into another term, give her the price, record it now), the timing (before the year runs out) and the authorisation boundary (the desk may make its own entries; Cedarloft's money moves by her hand). Given only when asked: the callback number 3125550162, the account number 610733, the tax digits 1182, the building's address, that the tier stays as it is, that no purchase order is needed, that nothing is in dispute, and a flat refusal to guess at internal references. Reacted to only after the agent says something: she is taken aback to hear the account is behind and coverage is off, then authorises and makes the payment herself and reads the reference back. Her natural trap is her own tracker figure, "a little over thirteen thousand" — close to the 12854 an agent gets from the computation document alone and far from gold, so an agent that has quietly skipped the factors will hear no objection at all. Nothing in the text names a prerequisite. Her last reaction answers the last gold action: she reads the renewed price back, notes it for the budget and rings off, asking for nothing further.

THE CHAIN THE AGENT MUST DISCOVER, AND ITS BREADTH
Depth: surface goal (renew the term) -> the renewal rule's prerequisite sentence -> the agreement does not stand back in force -> the reinstatement policy -> its own prerequisite sentence -> the arrears have not been cleared -> the clearance policy, which is the owner's own act. Three hops, and the order cannot be swapped: pricing the renewal first gives a figure taken on an agreement the policy does not allow it on, and charging the reinstatement first gives 290.00 instead of 230.00.
Breadth: the three computations together read the instalment ledger under two different windows, the payment ledger under two windows, the charge ledger filtered to charges for instalments left unpaid, the visit bookings and completions under a three-month window and over the whole term, the term's entitlement credit, the preventive completions against the written reports, the agreement's withdrawal day and term end day, and four separate fields of the owner's building automation service plan at the same building.

EASY MISTAKES, AND HOW THE POLICY EXCLUDES THEM
Escalating the annual price in force at the published rate: the base rule says the escalation acts on what the term delivered, and this term ran two visits short. Applying the tier's 3.0 percent: two charges for instalments left unpaid stand on the agreement, which puts the escalation on its middle tier. Taking the whole-ledger arrears of 3380.00 as the clearance figure: the arrears follow the billing cycle, and twelve instalments a year means the last three months. Taking the reinstatement fee in full: the shortfall after the clearance is inside one instalment. Counting both unperformed bookings as lost visits: the window a 42-day withdrawal sets is three months, and one of them was booked 2026-08-18. Taking the bundle credit at half: the plan still carries alarm responses.

STANDARD SOLUTION
Find the account, verify, read the agreement, read its whole history, read the intake records, read the owner's automation plan at the building. Compute the clearance figure (3030.60), unlock the owner's own clearance action, hand it over and let her pay it by bank transfer. Compute the charge for restoring coverage on the world that payment leaves (230.00) and put coverage back in force. Compute the renewal price on the world after that (10948) and record the further term.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN (round 2 figures; the round 1 run is superseded)
The verification script evaluates each policy's compute on initial_state plus the gold writes already landed, applies the real task tool between steps, substitutes each factor's baseline and all baselines at once, then replays with the prerequisite write skipped.
  .venv/bin/python <scratchpad>/maint_rework_wz/calc1.py <scratchpad>/maint_rework_wz/seed1.json
  maintenance_ext_renewal_arrears_clearance  result 3030.6   baseline 3411.2   factor baselines: arrears_cycle_window 3290.6 | withdrawn_coverage_share 3046.2 | withdrawal_handling_charge 2985.6 | portfolio_standing_allowance 3180.6
  maintenance_ext_coverage_reinstatement     result 230.0    baseline 400.0    factor baselines: cleared_account_share 290.0 | remaining_term_bearing 350.0 | lost_visit_window 740.0 | lost_visit_remobilisation 60.0 | automation_plan_discount 350.0
  maintenance_ext_renewal_term_pricing       result 10948.0  baseline 12854.0  factor baselines: term_conduct_escalation 10783.0 | delivered_term_base 11609.0 | automation_reach_discount 11811.0 | alarm_watch_bundle_credit 11548.0 | behind_account_surcharge 10728.0 | report_shortfall_adjustment 11088.0
  prerequisite skip run: skip the clearance -> the reinstatement charge recomputes to 290.0 instead of 230.0
  tool receipts returned in order, the agreement finishing in its renewed term running 2027-01-01 to 2027-12-31 at 10948.00 a year, standing active.
Every one of those figures is what computations[] carries, and the three results are exactly the three gold arguments.

FORWARD AND REVERSE SWEEP, rule <-> compute_basis <-> compute
Forward: every binding that reads the world, aggregates, branches or rounds carries a verbatim quotation of the rule sentence that legislates it, checked mechanically by re-reading each compute_basis value out of the policy's own rule after whitespace normalisation, for all three policies, with no misses. Sensitive-word cross-check: quotations saying "in the last three months" / "in the last nine months" / "in the last six months" sit on expressions carrying within_months=3, 9 and 6; "at the single clearance share" and "at the part cleared share" sit on multiplications by K constants; "rounded to the nearest cent once, on the final result alone" sits on the single RND at the result of the first two policies and "rounded to the nearest whole dollar once, on the final result alone" on the RND(..., 0) of the third; "the higher of the two stands" sits on MX with the tier's floor; "never falls below nothing" sits on MX(0, ...).
Reverse: reading each rule through, every load-bearing sentence is claimed. The opening paragraph of each policy is its baseline and is claimed by the plain bindings and the result; every ladder sentence is claimed by its factor's decides binding; the two prerequisite sentences are claimed not by compute but by the two declared edges, which is where they belong. No sentence promises a window, filter, branch, order or rounding that compute does not implement, and no expression carries a filter the rule does not state. The order and grouping of the renewal arithmetic is pinned in prose sentence by sentence — the base raised first, then the discount taken off the escalated figure, then the bundle credit off what the discount leaves, then the surcharge added and the adjustment subtracted, then the floor tested, then one rounding — because every one of those choices moves the number.

SOLVABILITY EVIDENCE AGAINST GOLD
Steps 7 and 9 are state_due and cite pre-action initial_state rows (and, for step 9, the prior step that changed the shortfall) as their intent source, never the caller: the money was owed and the coverage was withdrawn whether or not anyone rang. Step 11 is on_request and cites the caller's own words verbatim, with the discriminator phrase "the further term actually recorded against the agreement" occurring verbatim in the cited snippet. Every base policy governing each write subject appears in base_preconditions, with policy_scope where base carries no gate on that subject and the full evidence-binding chain where it does: the reinstatement window gate correlated by agreement_id, and both renewal gates correlated by the intake record's agreement_id, each bound to the action's agreement_id argument. Stage provenance: the clearance is performed_by_this_tool, the reinstatement is established_by_prior_tool citing prior_step 7, and the renewal is preexisting_before_conversation citing the intake record received 2026-11-04. Nothing in this task turns a status registration into a real-world event: the money moves on the call, coverage is restored by the office's own act, and the further term is recorded against an acceptance already on file. All three writes land synchronously under the single frozen_time of 2026-11-19 14:05:00 CST.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT ALONE
Masking the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this dossier, and working only from the policy prose as it will be published, the tool schemas, the rows the share finders return and the caller's actual lines: the caller wants a renewal; the renewal rule says a further term is recorded only once the agreement stands back in force after a withdrawal, and the agreement record shows it withdrawn; the reinstatement rule says its charge is worked out only after a payment against the agreement as a whole answers the arrears, and the ledger shows no such payment; so the writes run clearance, reinstatement, renewal, and each parameter is forced (the agreement is the only one at the building the caller names, the payment channel is the one she states, and each amount follows from the rules and the rows). Recomputing the three amounts by hand off the visible rows gives 3030.60, 230.00 and 10948 — the same as gold, with no second reading available at any step.


ROUND 2 REWORK — AUDIT ITEMS AND WHAT CHANGED (audits/policy_task/maintenance_agreement_desk, first revision)
- G-3 / F-1-1 (the term-share ladder had two tiers selecting the same value): the ladder now runs monotone with three distinct outcomes — more than six whole months left, the whole of the fee; one to six months left, the part term share; no whole month left, a new residual term share — the fall-through being the whole, which is what the computation document states. This world still sits on the middle tier (one whole month left), so the charge is unchanged, but the factor is now drawn from a real partition of outcomes.
- G-2 (no-access closures counted as completed visits): the reinstatement rule now states that a booking the office attended and closed as a no-access call is taken as answered and is never counted as lost, and the renewal rule now states that such a closure consumes none of the visits credited and is not counted among the visits completed, with compute subtracting those rows; no consequence on this world, which has no no-access row.
- O-3 (an advance on the reinstatement fee collected at clearance and never netted): the clearance policy no longer collects any part of the reinstatement fee. In its place it carries a withdrawal handling charge of its own, tiered by how long coverage stood withdrawn, so the reinstatement fee is taken once, by the reinstatement policy alone. The clearance figure moved from 3185.60 to 3030.60 and the shortfall the reinstatement fee is taken on from 194.40 to 349.40, still inside one instalment.
- O-5 (action-form edge where a state form was available): the reinstatement policy's prerequisite sentence is now in the state form, waiting on a payment recorded against the agreement as a whole rather than against any named invoice — the record-visible distinction the auditor named — and the edge carries no fallback_reason.
- O-6 (the reinstatement tool returns the agreement to pending_renewal, an edge absent from the base lifecycle): kept. Coverage was withdrawn from inside the renewal window (renewal_notice_date 2026-10-02 precedes the withdrawal), base names pending_renewal -> suspended as a transition, and putting coverage "back in force" restores the standing it was withdrawn from; the only alternative, active, would leave the renewal with no base transition to run from. No agent choice depends on the target standing, the tool contract states it, and it is recorded here as a declared refinement of the lifecycle rather than a silent one.
- O-7 (base multi-site discount at renewal neither applied nor declared away): kept as designed; the owner holds one agreement, so the count never reaches the tier's threshold of 3 and the discount is nil on this world, and the renewal policy's overwrite names only the escalation-order sentence, leaving the multi-site rule in force at nil.
- O-10 (E-3, E-5): the renewal's surcharge test now compares the withdrawal day with the term start day, so "withdrawn in the term" is what compute reads; every controls-plan read in the three policies is now scoped to the agreement's building, so "the plan at the building" is what compute reads.
- Boundary observation: the withdrawal day moved from 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-08, so coverage has stood withdrawn 42 days at the handling day — still on the 31-to-60-day tiers of the clearance and the lost-visit window — and the tier's 45-day for-cause period has three days to run rather than none.
user_scenario:
Priya Raghunathan looks after the physical assets in Cedarloft Asset Management, LLC's medical portfolio. She is warm, fast-talking, and reads from a renewal tracker she keeps herself; she has no visibility of what accounts payable does with the invoices and says so cheerfully if it ever comes up. She is ringing the Halvorsen client services desk on a Thursday afternoon between two site walks.

Her reason is straightforward and she gives it in the first breath: she wants the maintenance agreement at the Larkspur Medical Plaza carried into another term before the year runs out. She posted the signed renewal acceptance back a couple of weeks ago and has heard nothing since, and what she needs today is the price for the coming year and the further term actually recorded against the agreement, not a note in someone's file to deal with in January. She is content for the desk to make whatever entries its own side needs; where money has to come from Cedarloft she will move it herself from the bank rather than hand anyone the details, and she says so plainly.

Asked who is calling, she gives her name and Cedarloft Asset Management, LLC, and if the desk needs something to look the account up with she offers the number they call her on, 3125550162. When she is asked to confirm herself before anything is touched she reads the account number 610733 off the renewal notice in front of her, and adds the last four of the company's federal tax number, 1182, if a second detail is wanted. She has the billing address on the letterhead and can read it out if the desk insists on a third.

The rest comes out only when she is asked. The building is the Larkspur Medical Plaza on Larkspur Court in Naperville. The tier stays as it is; she has no appetite for changing what the agreement covers and says the coverage has been right for the building. No purchase order is needed on the invoices, that is not how Cedarloft works. If the desk asks whether anything on the account is in dispute she says nothing is, as far as she knows, and that she does not see the invoices herself. Internal reference numbers she cannot give at all and will say so rather than guess.

If the agent tells her the account is behind and that coverage at the building has been switched off, she is genuinely taken aback for a moment — nobody told her — and then becomes brisk about it: she says she is authorised to settle it on the spot, asks for the figure, and moves the money herself by bank transfer from the operating account once the desk has given her the means to do it. She reads back the confirmation reference the payment returns. She does not ask how the figure was arrived at and does not argue with it; she only wants coverage back on and the renewal done.

She has one soft check of her own, from the renewal tracker: she remembers next year being pencilled in at a little over thirteen thousand, and if the price she is read is far away from that she says so and asks the desk to look at it again against the agreement before she writes it into the budget. She will not say what it should be, because she does not know how the office prices a renewal.

When the agent tells her the further term has been recorded and gives her the price for it, she reads the figure back, says that is what she needed for the budget, thanks them for picking it all up on one call, and rings off.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the building owner's account record from the company and the callback number the caller states.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing on the agreement can be read or written until the owner's account record is in hand; it carries the customer reference every later lookup is scoped by.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Record a passing in-session identity check against the account on file using the two details the caller reads out.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No payment, charge or change of term may be recorded on the agreement until the caller has been verified against the account record.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the owner's maintenance agreements: the tier held, the lifecycle standing, the term dates, the day coverage was withdrawn, the covered unit count, the annual price in force and the balance owed.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The lifecycle standing, the day coverage was withdrawn, the term end day and the annual price in force are inputs of all three of this call's computations, and the standing is what shows the renewal cannot yet be recorded.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Pull the agreement's whole history: every instalment invoiced with its due day, every payment received, the charges for instalments left unpaid, the entitlement credited for the term, and every visit booked, completed or reported.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every history aggregate in this call is taken over these rows — the instalments due in the last three months against the payments received in them, the whole instalment and payment ledgers, the count and value of the charges for instalments left unpaid, the visits booked and completed over three months and over the term, the visits the term credited and the preventive completions without a written report.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read what the owner has lodged on this agreement: the signed renewal acceptance, when it reached the office and the day it takes effect.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: A further term may be recorded only where a renewal acceptance from the customer is on file, and the same record is what shows no non-renewal notice was ever received.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the owner's building automation service plan at the same building: its standing, the monitored points it covers, the support hours still in its pool, the alarm responses still in its allowance and what it owes on its own balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan's standing and its balance decide the allowance in the clearance figure, its support pool decides the discount on the charge for restoring coverage, and its monitored points and alarm allowance decide the portfolio discount and the bundle credit in the renewal price.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the customer's own action for clearing the arrears standing on the agreement, so it can be handed to the caller.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Clearing the arrears is the owner's own act on the owner's own money; the desk unlocks it and hands it over rather than performing it, and this unlock has no effect on the records.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The building owner clears the arrears standing on the agreement herself, by bank transfer, as one figure for the whole account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: maintenance_ext_renewal_arrears_clearance is the only policy that computes clearance_amount_usd, and the charge for restoring coverage is worked out on the shortfall this payment leaves.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.agreement_id: The Larkspur agreement's own reference number, read from the maintenance agreement lookup at step 2 and handed to the caller with the action; it is the only maintenance agreement the owner holds at the Larkspur Medical Plaza, which is the building the caller names.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.clearance_amount_usd: 3030.60. The agreement is billed in twelve instalments a year, so the arrears are the instalments that fell due in the last three months — the 2026-08, 2026-09 and 2026-10 instalments at 1040.00 each, the 2026-07 instalment having fallen due 2026-07-31, more than three months back — less the payments received in those three months, of which there are none, the last payment having reached the office 2026-07-29: 3120.00. Coverage stands suspended and two charges for instalments left unpaid stand on the agreement, so those charges, 31.20 together, are added at the single clearance share of 0.5, giving 15.60. Coverage has stood suspended since 2026-10-08, that is 42 days, more than thirty and no more than sixty, so the withdrawal handling charge of 45.00 is carried. The building automation service plan at the building stands active and owes nothing on its own balance, so the standing allowance of 150.00 is earned. 3120.00 + 15.60 + 45.00 - 150.00, rounded once at the end, is 3030.60.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_method: ach. Basis: the tool's own contract fixes the closed set and says of this value 'ach - the owner has pushed the money by bank transfer from their own bank.' Uniqueness: the caller says she 'moves the money herself by bank transfer from the operating account', which is the bank-transfer value and no other; check is a paper cheque, credit_card is a company card and wire is a same-day wire, none of which she offers.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden desk action that puts withdrawn coverage back in force and charges for doing it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it has no effect on the records and happens once for this action in the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Put the agreement's coverage back in force, returning it to the renewal window it was withdrawn from, and book the charge for restoring it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: maintenance_ext_coverage_reinstatement is the only policy that computes reinstatement_charge_usd, and a further term may not be recorded while the agreement still stands withdrawn.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.agreement_id: The Larkspur agreement's own reference number, read from the maintenance agreement lookup at step 2; it is the agreement whose coverage stands withdrawn and the only one the owner holds at that building.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.reinstatement_charge_usd: 230.00. After the owner's clearance the payments received on the agreement stand at 10050.60 against 10400.00 invoiced, a shortfall of 349.40, which is no more than the value of one instalment of the annual price in force (12480.00 over twelve, that is 1040.00), so the tier's reinstatement fee of 400.00 is taken at the part cleared share of 0.75, giving 300.00. One whole month of the term remains at the reinstatement day, between one and six, so the part term share of 0.6 is borne: 300.00 x 0.6 = 180.00. Coverage stood withdrawn for 42 days, more than thirty and no more than sixty, so the visits counted as lost are those booked for a day in the last three months with no visit completed against them: two were booked in that window, on 2026-09-22 and 2026-10-20, and one completion falls in it, so exactly one visit is counted as lost and the tier's price for one additional visit, 340.00, is added at the half visit share, giving 170.00. The building automation service plan at the building stands active and still carries support hours in its pool, so the plan discount of 120.00 is taken off. 180.00 + 170.00 - 120.00, rounded once at the end, is 230.00.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden desk action that records a further term on the agreement at the price settled for it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock/call pair; it has no effect on the records and happens once for this action in the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Roll the agreement into a further term of the same length at the price settled for it, replacing the annual price in force and returning the agreement to active.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: maintenance_ext_renewal_term_pricing is the only policy that computes renewed_annual_price_usd, and recording the further term is what the caller rang for.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.agreement_id: The Larkspur agreement's own reference number, read from the maintenance agreement lookup at step 2; it is the agreement the caller's renewal acceptance was lodged against and the only one she holds at that building.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.renewed_annual_price_usd: 10948.00. The base the escalation acts on follows what the term delivered: the term credited 10 visits and 8 completions stand on the agreement, two short, so the base is the annual price in force less the tier's price for one additional visit for each visit short: 12480.00 - 2 x 340.00 = 11800.00. Two charges for instalments left unpaid stand on the agreement, so the standing escalation of 4.5 percent is applied rather than the tier's published 3.0: 11800.00 x 1.045 = 12331.00. The building's automation service plan stands active and covers 240 monitored points, two hundred or more, so the full portfolio discount share of 0.07 is taken off the escalated figure: 12331.00 x 0.93 = 11467.83. That plan still carries 3 alarm responses in its allowance, so the tier's bundle credit of 600.00 is taken off in full, leaving 10867.83. Coverage stood withdrawn in the term and eight payments have been received on the agreement, six or more, so the part arrears surcharge of 220.00 is carried. Exactly one preventive visit completed in the term carries no written condition report, so the single report adjustment of 140.00 is earned. 10867.83 + 220.00 - 140.00 is 10947.83, which stands above the tier's annual price floor of 6000.00 and rounds once at the end to 10948.

edges.policy_source: A further term is recorded only once the agreement stands back in force after a withdrawal of coverage.

edges.policy_source: The charge for putting coverage back in force is worked out only after the arrears standing on the agreement are answered by a payment recorded against the agreement as a whole rather than against any named invoice.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The ledger carries 10400.00 of instalments invoiced against 7020.00 of payments received — seven payments, every one of them applied to a named invoice, the April one 260.00 short — leaving a shortfall of 3380.00, far more than the 1040.00 value of one instalment; no payment recorded against the agreement as a whole stands on it, and the arrears stand unanswered at the handling day.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the owner's clearance of 3030.60 is booked as one figure against the agreement with no invoice named, the payments received stand at 10050.60 against 10400.00 invoiced, a shortfall of 349.40, which is no more than one instalment, so the reinstatement fee is taken at the part cleared share of 0.75 rather than in full and the charge falls from 290.00 to 230.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, not a fan: the renewal waits on the reinstatement and the reinstatement waits on the owner's clearance, so there is only one order the three writes can take and no reordering to prove. Each policy's own rule states its single wait outright — the renewal's 'A further term is recorded only once the agreement stands back in force after a withdrawal of coverage.' and the reinstatement's 'The charge for putting coverage back in force is worked out only after the arrears standing on the agreement are answered by a payment recorded against the agreement as a whole rather than against any named invoice.' — so the order is entailed by the policy text rather than chosen by the author.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the reinstatement leaves the agreement standing suspended with no day of restoration and no charge for restoring coverage on its balance, so the terminal record differs in maintenance_agreements.status (suspended instead of active on the renewed term), in reinstatement_date (empty instead of 2026-11-19), in balance_due (lower by the 230.00 charge) and by one missing charge row in the history; the renewal is then recorded against an agreement the policy does not allow it on.

Skipping the owner's clearance and replaying everything else leaves the charge for restoring coverage at 290.00 instead of 230.00: the shortfall between the instalments invoiced and the payments received stays at 3380.00, more than one instalment, so the tier's reinstatement fee is taken in full rather than at the part cleared share.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona never mentions arrears, a withdrawal of coverage, a charge for restoring it, or anything that has to be done first. Her opening is the renewal and nothing else: the price for the coming year and the further term recorded. She is written as the asset manager who signed the renewal and who has no sight of the invoices, and she says so, so her silence about the arrears is in character rather than coy. Everything she contributes about the arrears is a passive reaction that fires only after the agent has told her the account is behind and coverage is off — she is taken aback, then authorises and makes the payment herself. Her one volunteered figure is a little over thirteen thousand from her own renewal tracker, which is her own pencilled estimate and points at none of the prerequisites; if the agent never finds them she still takes whatever price she is read and closes the call.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: renew_agreement_term_748887d3 looks up the agreement only to read its current term dates, then writes the new term dates, the new price and the standing; it reads no status, tests no arrears, and rolls the term over whatever the agreement stands at, so an agent that skips the reinstatement still gets a receipt. reinstate_agreement_coverage_5877576a likewise writes the standing, the day of restoration and the charge without testing whether any payment has been received, and clear_agreement_arrears_489edb92 books the owner's payment without testing what is owed. The only refusal any of the three carries is for an agreement reference that names no record at all. The cost of leaving a prerequisite unresolved shows up in the renewal price, the reinstatement charge and the terminal record, never in a tool refusal.

remaining_term_bearing (parameter): one whole month of the term remains at the reinstatement day, between one and six, so the part term share of 0.6 is borne. Baseline: the full term share, which would have given 350.00.

lost_visit_window (method): coverage stood withdrawn for 42 days, more than thirty and no more than sixty, so the visits counted as lost are those booked for a day in the last three months with no visit completed against them — two booked (2026-09-22 and 2026-10-20) against one completion in that window — giving one. lost_visit_remobilisation (method): exactly one visit is counted as lost, so the tier's price for one additional visit, 340.00, is added at the half visit share, giving 170.00. Baseline: nothing added, which would have given 60.00.

automation_plan_discount (parameter, cross-difficulty): the owner's building automation service plan stands active and still carries 6.5 support hours in its pool, so the plan discount of 120.00 is taken off. Baseline: no discount, which would have given 350.00.
